# Volume 3 — Chapter XXVI Enter Rowena

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

The female students at Tabby’s Place were getting outfitted for the party that the Juniors were throwing in honor of the Seniors in February. Nell looked at her reflection in the blue room's glass with feminine pleasure. Her dress was especially lovely. At first, it had been nothing more than an unpretentious small underdress of cream silk beneath a chiffon overdress. However, Cressy had demanded that she carry it to her own house during the Christmas break to stitch minuscule rosebuds across the entire chiffon. Cressy possessed skillful hands, and her work produced a gown that all the other Wexcombe girls coveted. Allie Boone herself, who possessed Parisian frocks, was accustomed to gazing with yearning upon that rosebud creation whenever Nell walked up the principal staircase at Wexcombe wearing it.
{: #nw-v03-c26-p0000 }

Nell was testing how a white orchid looked in her hair. White orchids had been sent to her by Cyril Lisle for the reception, and she was aware that no other Wexcombe girl would wear them that evening—when Cressy entered, looking on with admiration.
{: #nw-v03-c26-p0001 }

“Nell, you are undoubtedly looking handsome tonight. For nine out of ten evenings, I am able to outshine you without difficulty. On that tenth one, you abruptly bloom into a figure that completely overshadows me. By what means do you achieve it?”
{: #nw-v03-c26-p0002 }

“The attire is responsible, my love. Superior plumage.”
{: #nw-v03-c26-p0003 }

“It is not. Your old blue flannel shirtwaist, which Mrs. Sowerby constructed for you, was what you had on the previous time you burst into gorgeousness. Had Cyril not lost his mind and affection for you previously, this evening would surely have accomplished it. However, I am disinclined to see orchids on you, Nell. Nay, jealousy is not the reason. You do not appear to match orchids. Their nature is excessively exotic—far too tropical—overly insolent. At all events, refrain from placing them in your hair.”
{: #nw-v03-c26-p0004 }

“Indeed, I shall not. I must confess to having no personal liking for orchids. It is my belief that they hold no relation to me. Such blooms are rarely dispatched by Cyril—he understands my preference for blossoms suited to daily companionship. One can merely pay a call to orchids.”
{: #nw-v03-c26-p0005 }

“Ezra gave me a few lovely pink rosebuds to wear tonight—however—he will not be attending. He claimed he was required to conduct a slum prayer-meeting! I doubt he desired to attend. Nell, I am terribly concerned that Ezra has no genuine feelings for me. And I am attempting to determine if I should waste away and perish, or proceed to obtain my B.A. and prove sensible and helpful.”
{: #nw-v03-c26-p0006 }

“Cressy, since you are completely incapable of being useful and sensible, it would be better if you just wasted away and died,” Nell remarked with cruelty.
{: #nw-v03-c26-p0007 }

“Heartless Nell!”
{: #nw-v03-c26-p0008 }

“You foolish Cressy! It is perfectly clear to you that Ezra holds affection for you.”
{: #nw-v03-c26-p0009 }

“However—he refuses to say as much to me. And I am unable to force him. He appears to, I must confess. Nevertheless, silent gazes are not a truly trustworthy basis for decorating doilies and stitching borders on tablecloths. I prefer not to start those tasks before I am officially engaged. Doing so would invite bad luck.”
{: #nw-v03-c26-p0010 }

“Cressy, Mr. Hale fears asking for your hand in marriage. Because he lacks wealth, he is unable to provide a dwelling like the one you have always possessed. That single motive has prevented him from speaking up until now, as you well know.”
{: #nw-v03-c26-p0011 }

“I guess that’s true,” Cressy conceded sorrowfully. “Well”—cheering a bit—“should he fail to propose to me, I’ll propose to him, simple as that. Consequently, everything will turn out fine. I refuse to fret. On another note, Hugh Carrow spends all his time with Rowena Calder. Were you aware?”
{: #nw-v03-c26-p0012 }

Nell was attempting to secure a small chain made of gold around her neck. The fastener unexpectedly proved troublesome to handle. Was something wrong with the mechanism—or perhaps with her own hands?
{: #nw-v03-c26-p0013 }

“No,” she casually replied. “Rowena Calder, who is that?”
{: #nw-v03-c26-p0014 }

“She is the sister of Ronald Calder. This winter, she is located in Portmaris to study music. Although I have not set eyes on her, people claim she possesses great beauty and that Hugh is utterly infatuated with her. Nell, I felt so much anger when you turned down Hugh. Yet Cyril Lisle was your destiny. That is clear to me now. Ultimately, you were correct.”
{: #nw-v03-c26-p0015 }

Nell refrained from blushing, contrary to her customary reaction whenever the girls took it for granted that her future wedding with Cyril Lisle was a done deal. Suddenly, she experienced a sense of dullness. The talking of Cressy appeared unimportant, and she found the reception tiresome. She struck poor Smudge’s ears.
{: #nw-v03-c26-p0016 }

“Get off that cushion this second, you cat, you! Why do you not stay down where you are supposed to be?”
{: #nw-v03-c26-p0017 }

Gathering up her orchids, Nell headed to the lower floor, where Aunt Euphemia was overseeing a line of coats suspended in front of the hearth to get warm. Cyril Lisle was standing by for Nell, entertaining himself by bothering the Sarah-cat as he stood there. He was not favored by the Sarah-cat. Her back was invariably turned to him. On the other hand, all the other residents at Tabby’s Place held him in high regard. Aunt Euphemia, completely won over by his constant and respectful manners, along with the appealing cadence of his lovely voice, pronounced that he was the finest young gentleman she had ever met, and that Nell was an exceedingly lucky young woman. Nell felt uneasy when such comments were made. It was true that Cyril’s courtship had possessed all the romance a young woman’s heart could want, but—she preferred that Aunt Euphemia and the girls would refrain from assuming everything was settled. As Cyril whispered a poetic praise while assisting her into her coat, her face did not flush nor did she feel the customary flutter; furthermore, he noticed her reticence throughout their short stroll to Wexcombe. It appeared to him that her complexion was somewhat pale upon leaving the coeds’ dressing room; nevertheless, the moment they stepped into the reception room, her vivacity and vivid hue abruptly reappeared. The look she bestowed on Cyril was her most joyful. He answered her glance with a smile containing what Cressy termed “his deep, black, velvety smile.” Even so, her eyes were not truly fixed on Cyril. She possessed a sharp awareness that Hugh was positioned beneath the palms directly across the hall, engaged in conversation with a young woman who had to be Rowena Calder.
{: #nw-v03-c26-p0018 }

Her beauty was striking, possessing a grand elegance that would eventually turn somewhat heavy in her later years. She was a lofty young woman, featuring expansive navy eyes, pale complexion contours, and a dark sheen upon her sleek tresses.
{: #nw-v03-c26-p0019 }

“She appears exactly how I have forever wished to appear,” Nell reflected in despair. “Complexion of a rose leaf—violet eyes like stars—hair as black as a raven—indeed, every single one is hers. It is surprising that she is not additionally named Lucinda Fitzgerald! However, I doubt that her form equals mine, and without question her nose does not.”
{: #nw-v03-c26-p0020 }

This deduction brought a slight sense of relief to Nell.
{: #nw-v03-c26-p0021 }
